claims.head: Who drives the play: the Sabres
claims.body: At 5-on-5, the Sabres have been around the middle of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Sharks one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Sabres’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.
claims.call: The Sabres get the bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances.
claims.nums: Share of 5-on-5 expected goals: Buffalo 51.1%, San Jose 45.0%
claims.gist: The Sabres usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.

claims.head: Bruisers vs. Finesse
claims.body: The Sharks hit a lot, but the Sabres mostly don’t. San Jose is one of the league’s best for physicality, and Buffalo is near the bottom. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Sharks.

SJS.head: The Sharks have a hill to climb
SJS.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage, Buffalo has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sharks’ best way through is a power play that gets going.

BUF.head: The Sabres have a lot going for them
BUF.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage, Buffalo has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sharks can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

items.text: Michael Kesselring faces his old team, Buffalo.
The Sabres have been without Alex Lyon all season. Colten Ellis is expected to start.
The Sharks are newly without Igor Chernyshov, and have been without Alexander Wennberg since Oct 19.
Mason Marchment is two goals from 100.
